Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer with its own UI under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. It has an app guide in `docs/guide` that people read (on GitHub and in the app under Help › JusPrin guide…) and that the in-app AI reads as skills. Before each release the guide is brought in line with the app by one command, `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`: it drives the built app through each page's screens with the shell harness, retakes the pictures, rebuilds the AI's copy of each page, checks every quoted on-screen label against the source, and asks the model each page's questions. The steps are in `docs/guide/README.md` under "Before a release", and one line under "Documentation" in `AGENTS.md` points to it.

All of this is on branch `claude/guide-window` (pushed to origin; not merged into `jusprin-dev`; no pull request). Another session is writing six more guide pages from that branch on `claude/hungry-murdock-3137cd`, and it also touches `docs/guide/README.md` and possibly `AGENTS.md`.

The problem this task solves: an agent making a release has no reason to open either of those files, so the guide step can be forgotten. The release steps are written only in the comment at the top of `.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml`, and that workflow already teaches by refusing: its `prepare` job has a step "Require the release notes" that stops with a message saying which file to write when `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md` is missing. The version comes from `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp` through `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.mjs`, whose checks are tested without GitHub by `release.test.mjs` beside it.

What Kenneth has agreed, relayed from a side conversation on 2026-11-11 in which he was asked "Should the release workflow refuse a release until the guide check has been run for that version?" and how he could override a refusal: the refusal exists, and its override is a tick box. His words: "override exists as The tick box. tell the main session to create a task chip to implement it". Everything more specific than those two points is a proposal he has not approved.

Kenneth wants this kept simple; his words about the guide process were "I don't want it to be too complicated and fancy." His communication rules are in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and the project's in `AGENTS.md`: full sentences, no invented labels, proposals marked as proposals, decisions asked in full starting with "Decision needed", outcomes reported with what was tested, under about 500 words.

Task:
Make the JusPrin release workflow refuse to make a release until the guide check has been run for the version being released, with a tick box on the workflow's start form that overrides the refusal. Work on top of `claude/guide-window`, in your own worktree and branch.

Agreed by Kenneth: the refusal, and that its override is a tick box. The details below are proposals; build them unless the code shows a better way, and say in your report which details were your choice.

1. The record. When `scripts/check_guide.py` passes, it writes a one-line record of the app version it was run for, the version in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`. Decide where the file lives and what it holds, keep it one small committed file, and write it only when every step the command ran passed. Think about which runs should count: a run with `--skip-app` or `--area` did not check the whole guide in the app.
2. The refusal. In `.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml`, in the `prepare` job beside "Require the release notes", compare the record with the version being released. If they differ, stop with a message that says what to do: run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai` on a built copy of this commit, commit the result, see `docs/guide/README.md`. Put the comparison where `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.test.mjs` can cover it, as the other release checks in `release.mjs` are, and add tests for it.
3. The override. A second boolean input on the Run workflow form beside `sign_macos`, worded something like "Release without the guide check". Ticked, the workflow skips the refusal and prints a warning in the run that the guide was not checked for this version. Also proposed: the draft release's title says so, the way an unsigned draft's title already says it is unsigned.
4. The words. One line in the workflow's top comment next to the line about release notes, and a short "Releasing" section in `AGENTS.md` that lists what a release needs in one place: the version, the release notes, the guide check. The line now under "Documentation" in `AGENTS.md` about `docs/guide/` moves there. Update `docs/guide/README.md` so its "Before a release" steps mention the record and the refusal.

Points to carry, each still a proposal:
- The workflow can also be started by pushing a branch named `jusprin-release/<anything>`, and a push has no form. The proposal is to keep the refusal on for that route too, so a pushed release without the guide check needs the record edited by hand. Kenneth was told this and did not comment. Ask him as a full decision if it matters to how you build it.
- The refusal makes forgetting impossible, not skipping: the record can be edited by hand and the step can be removed from the workflow file, as is true of the release notes refusal today. Do not add machinery to prevent that.
- The record proves someone ran the check for that version, not that it ran on the final commit. Say so in the words you write; do not try to solve it.
- The session writing the remaining guide pages works from the same branch and touches `docs/guide/README.md` and possibly `AGENTS.md`. Keep your changes to those two files small and expect to rebase.

Testing. Run `node --test src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.test.mjs` and show the new check failing before it passes. Run `scripts/check_guide.py --skip-app` to confirm the command still works and behaves as you decided about the record; a full run needs the harness built, which is a 30-minute build, so only do it if your change to the command cannot be verified otherwise, and follow the shared-machine build rules in `AGENTS.md` if you do. The workflow itself runs only for the release publisher, so a real run needs Kenneth: check the workflow file's syntax as far as you can without running it, and say plainly in your report that it has not been run on GitHub.

Do not push, open a pull request, or run the release workflow unless Kenneth asks. Done looks like: the record, the refusal with its message, the tick box, and the words are in place on your branch; the release tests pass; and your report says what was built, what was tested with the results, what could not be tested, and which details were your own choice.

name: JusPrin release

# Builds JusPrin from one commit and uploads the files to a DRAFT GitHub
# release. It never publishes anything.
#
# - The version is the one in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp, and
#   the draft is tagged jusprin/v<version>, as JusPrin 1.4.0 was (the repo
#   still holds OrcaSlicer's own v2.x tags). GitHub creates that tag only when
#   the draft is published, by hand, on the Releases page. JusPrin's update
#   check reads the public release list, which never includes drafts, so
#   users see nothing until then.
# - It stops if that version is already released, is not above every
#   released JusPrin version, or its tag already exists
#   (Packaging/release.mjs), and if
#   Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md, the notes the draft starts with and
#   that the app shows under "What's new", is missing.
# - Running it again for the same version replaces the draft's files.
# - Files: Windows x64 installer and portable zip, macOS universal disk image,
#   Linux x64 AppImage, and SHA256SUMS.txt.
# - Only the release publisher can run it: the repo variable
#   JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER, or kennethjiang when it is unset.
# - Signing: macOS when "sign_macos" is ticked, with the Apple secrets JusPrin
#   1.x used. Windows builds are unsigned. An unsigned draft says so in its
#   title.
#
# Start it from Actions > JusPrin release > Run workflow (the file must also
# be on the default branch for that button), or by pushing a branch named
# jusprin-release/<anything>.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sign_macos:
        description: 'Sign and notarise the macOS app with the Apple secrets'
        type: boolean
        default: false
  push:
    branches:
      - 'jusprin-release/**'

permissions:
  contents: write   # create the draft and upload its files
  actions: read

concurrency:
  group: jusprin-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    name: Check the version
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.check.outputs.tag }}
      prerelease: ${{ steps.check.outputs.prerelease }}
      draft_id: ${{ steps.check.outputs.draft_id }}
    steps:
      - name: Only the release publisher
        env:
          PUBLISHER: ${{ vars.JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER || 'kennethjiang' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_ACTOR" != "$PUBLISHER" ]; then
            echo "::error::Only @$PUBLISHER may make a JusPrin release (this run is @$GITHUB_ACTOR's)."
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          sparse-checkout: src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      - name: Test the release checks
        run: node --test src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.test.mjs

      - name: Check the version against the releases
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh api --paginate --slurp "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases?per_page=100" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/releases.json"
          gh api --paginate "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/matching-refs/tags/" --jq '.[].ref' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/tags.txt"
          node src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.mjs check src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/releases.json" "$RUNNER_TEMP/tags.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Require the release notes
        run: |
          notes="src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}.md"
          if [ ! -s "$notes" ]; then
            echo "::error::Write $notes first. The draft starts with it and the app shows it under What's new."
            exit 1
          fi
          if grep -q '^PLACEHOLDER' "$notes"; then
            echo "::warning::$notes is still the placeholder. Replace it before publishing the draft."
          fi

  build:
    name: Build
    needs: prepare
    uses: ./.github/workflows/jusprin_build_all.yml
    with:
      version: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
      sign_macos: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.sign_macos || false }}
    secrets: inherit

  draft:
    name: Upload to the draft release
    needs: [prepare, build]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Optional approval gate: give the "release" environment a required
    # reviewer in the repo settings.
    environment: release
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
      TAG: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.tag }}
      DRAFT_ID: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.draft_id }}
      PRERELEASE: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.prerelease }}
      SIGNED_MACOS: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.sign_macos || false }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          sparse-checkout: src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging

      - name: Collect the files
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: jusprin-*
          path: collected
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Checksums
        run: |
          mkdir dist
          # The per-architecture Mac bundles only feed the universal app.
          find collected -maxdepth 1 -type f ! -name 'JusPrin_Mac_bundle_*' -exec cp {} dist/ \;
          (cd dist && sha256sum -- * > SHA256SUMS.txt)
          cat dist/SHA256SUMS.txt

      - name: Create or update the draft
        run: |
          title="JusPrin $VERSION"
          if [ "$SIGNED_MACOS" != "true" ]; then
            title="$title (UNSIGNED TEST BUILD: do not publish)"
          else
            title="$title (Windows unsigned)"
          fi
          notes="src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/$VERSION.md"
          prerelease=$([ "$PRERELEASE" = "true" ] && echo --prerelease || echo --prerelease=false)
          if [ -z "$DRAFT_ID" ]; then
            gh release create "$TAG" dist/* --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --draft $prerelease \
              --target "$GITHUB_SHA" --title "$title" --notes-file "$notes"
          else
            # Never touch a published release: release.mjs only reports drafts.
            is_draft=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/$DRAFT_ID" --jq .draft)
            if [ "$is_draft" != "true" ]; then
              echo "::error::Release $DRAFT_ID is no longer a draft."
              exit 1
            fi
            gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/$DRAFT_ID" \
              -f target_commitish="$GITHUB_SHA" -f name="$title" -F prerelease="$PRERELEASE" \
              -f body="$(cat "$notes")" > /dev/null
            gh release upload "$TAG" dist/* --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          fi
          gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases?per_page=20" \
            --jq ".[] | select(.tag_name == \"$TAG\") | {name, draft, prerelease, target_commitish, html_url, assets: [.assets[].name]}"

"""Checks the app guide (docs/guide) from end to end, and rebuilds what is
built from it. Run it after editing a page, and before a release.

  1. Walks each page's screens in the app as built and takes its pictures
     (tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py). Needs the shell_integration_harness
     and jusprin_web targets built from this checkout, and this computer's
     screen.
  2. Rebuilds the skill AI reads from each page, and checks that every label
     a page quotes is in the source, that every section has a run in step 1,
     that every picture is one step 1 took, and that every page has questions
     for step 3 (AgentUI's guide.test.ts).
  3. With --ask-ai: asks the model each page's questions and has a judge read
     the answers (tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py), on the Claude
     subscription unless told otherwise after `--`.

    scripts/check_guide.py
    scripts/check_guide.py --area print-settings --ask-ai
    scripts/check_guide.py --skip-app             steps 2 and 3 only
    scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai -- --runs 1   options after -- go to step 3

Exits 0 when every step it ran passed.
"""
import argparse
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
AGENT_UI = ROOT / "src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI"


def step(title, command, cwd=ROOT, env=None):
    print(f"\n== {title}\n   {' '.join(map(str, command))}", flush=True)
    return subprocess.run(command, cwd=cwd, env=env).returncode == 0


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Checks the app guide and rebuilds what is built from it.")
    parser.add_argument("--area", help="one page, by its file name without .md")
    parser.add_argument("--skip-app", action="store_true", help="do not run the app: no walk, no new pictures")
    parser.add_argument("--ask-ai", action="store_true", help="also ask the model each page's questions")
    parser.add_argument("rest", nargs="*", help="after --: options for the questions run")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    area = ["--area", args.area] if args.area else []
    npx = shutil.which("npx")
    if npx is None:
        sys.exit("npx is not on PATH: the page checks need node")

    results = {}
    if not args.skip_app:
        results["the app walk and pictures"] = step(
            "1/3 walking the pages in the app and taking their pictures",
            [sys.executable, ROOT / "tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py", *area])
    results["skills, labels, sections, pictures and questions"] = step(
        "2/3 rebuilding the skills AI reads and checking the pages",
        [npx, "vitest", "run", "src/guide.test.ts"], cwd=AGENT_UI,
        env=dict(os.environ, JUSPRIN_UPDATE_GUIDE_SKILLS="1"))
    if args.ask_ai:
        options = args.rest or ["--backend", "claude-cli", "--judge", "claude-cli"]
        # The questions run exits 2 when it has no baseline to compare with, which it never has.
        print("\n== 3/3 asking the model each page's questions", flush=True)
        asked = subprocess.run([sys.executable, ROOT / "tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py", *area, "--must-pass", "1", *options],
                               cwd=ROOT)
        results["the model's answers"] = asked.returncode == 0

    print()
    for name, passed in results.items():
        print(f"{'pass' if passed else 'FAIL'}: {name}")
    sys.exit(0 if all(results.values()) else 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# JusPrin guide

How to use JusPrin, one page per part of the app. The same pages are in the app, under Help › JusPrin guide…, in the order of the list below.

- [Seeing and changing print settings](print-settings.md)

## Before a release

The guide is brought in line with the app before each release, on a computer with the app built.

1. Build the app's test harness and pages from the commit to release: the `shell_integration_harness` and `jusprin_web` targets.
2. Leave the computer alone and run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai`. It takes about a minute a page, plus the questions.
3. Fix what it reports, then run it again until it passes:
   - **A label is on no screen.** The app's wording changed. Find the new wording in the app and correct the page.
   - **A run failed.** Open its log, which the command names. Either the screen no longer works as the page says, and the page needs correcting, or the harness expects something the app no longer does, and the harness needs correcting.
   - **A picture is blank.** The program that started the command may not record the screen. Grant it Screen Recording in the system's privacy settings and run again.
   - **AI answered a question wrongly.** Read its reply in the output. Usually the page is unclear or its first line does not say when to read it.
4. Look through what changed on screen since the last release (`git log <last release tag>..HEAD -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin`). The command finds what a page gets wrong. It cannot find a new screen or menu item that no page mentions, so add those by hand.
5. Commit the pages together with their pictures and the skills the command rebuilt.

## What the command does

1. **Walks the app and takes the pictures.** `tests/shell/guide_checks.json` names, for each page, the runs of the app's test harness that go through the screens the page describes, and the checks in each run the page depends on. `tests/shell/run_guide_checks.py` runs them in the app as built and copies the pictures a page uses into `pictures/<page>/`.
2. **Rebuilds the copy AI reads.** `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/guide.ts` builds a skill from each page.
3. **Checks each page**, in `guide.test.ts` beside it: every label in bold is in the app's source, every section has a run in step 1, every picture is one step 1 took, and the page has questions for step 4. `components/Guide.test.tsx` checks that the app's guide window lists every page and shows each with all its pictures and without the parts written for AI.
4. **Asks AI the page's questions** (`--ask-ai`). `tests/project_prompt/guide_questions.json` holds them with what a right answer says. `tests/project_prompt/run_guide_tests.py` asks the model and has a judge read the replies.

## Writing a page

- Start it with `<!-- ai-description: … -->`: one line, at most 300 bytes, saying when AI should read it.
- Put words that are only for AI in `<!-- ai: … -->`. They are hidden on this site.
- Use bold only for words that are on screen, exactly as they are on screen.
- A picture goes on a line of its own, as `![what it shows](pictures/<page>/<name>.png)`, and comes from a run named in `guide_checks.json`. AI's copy leaves it out.
- A picture is kept at twice the screen's size, and the guide window shows it at half, the size it has on screen. Mark a run's picture that the harness draws at the screen's own size with `"atScreenSize": true`, and the command doubles it.
- List a new page at the top of this file, or the guide window leaves it out.
- Give each `##` section a run in `guide_checks.json`.
- Add at least three questions for the page to `guide_questions.json`.
- AI's copy may hold at most 16 KiB. Split a page that grows past that.

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Branches

- `jusprin-dev` is the development branch. Start each change on a new branch from it and land the change there. It began at `975c703f08`, the merge of OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, and contains the earlier development branches `jusprin-newui` and `ui-walkthrough`; start nothing new on those.
- `main` is the stable branch and GitHub's default branch: the repository's front page, its issue forms, and the workflows GitHub runs on a schedule come from it.
  - Never force-push `main`, so that people who cloned the repository never have to force-pull. Only in an extreme case with no other way out, and with Kenneth's yes, may an admin lift the GitHub protection that blocks force pushes and deletion.
  - For now `main` is also the release branch: it moves forward from `jusprin-dev` when a version is released, and releases are built from it. This may change if a separate release branch is added later.
- `jusprin-v1` holds JusPrin 1, for fixes to that version only.
- `jusprin-v2-poc` holds the experiments described below.
- Take each OrcaSlicer release into `jusprin-dev` as `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` rule 10 describes.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

Build the Release configuration unless asked otherwise.

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config Release --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config Release --target all --

# Windows
cmake --build . --config Release --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

- Docs live in `docs/`; the high-level design of a subsystem goes in `docs/HLSD/<subsystem>.md`.
